newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dowa Mining to raise copper output in H1 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Dowa Mining to raise copper output in H1 1997/98.

text.p: Dowa Mining Co, Japan's fourth-largest copper and zinc refiner, said on Monday it planned to raise its refined copper output by 3.5 percent in the first half of 1997/98 from the prior half-year.

The increase in part reflects a boost in capacity last year at the company's Kosaka refinery, which was expected to more than offset output losses due to scheduled maintenance at the facility in late August, a spokeswoman said.
Refined zinc output was expected to fall, due to scheduled maintenance at the Akita refinery in the summer, while lead output was seen mostly steady.

Japan's eight non-ferrous metal refiners announce output plans at the beginning of each fiscal half-year. Nippon Mining and Metals Co last week announced plans to boost copper output by 1.0 percent in the coming half-year. The remaining companies are scheduled to release production plans later this week.
